pin_added.question: The conflation I think will bite you hardest. You hold NVDA equity; suppose you also hold NVDA converts and are short NVDA calls. That is three Instruments, one Issuer, and exactly ONE earnings event. If earnings hangs off the ticker you get three earnings blocks on the same morning; if it hangs off the Issuer you get one, with three position lines under it. Is Issuer a real object for you, or does your book only ever hold one instrument per company - in which case I should collapse these two and stop being clever?

'Prices' is doing at least three jobs: yesterday's official close, the pre-market last trade at 07:00, and whatever mark your books use for P&L. The overnight move needs two of them and the P&L needs a specific one - and if they disagree, your tearsheet contradicts the risk system, which is how people stop trusting it. Which mark is authoritative for the P&L number, and is it the same source the risk team uses?

I invented Story and you should decide whether it survives. On a busy morning one event generates ten wire items. Without Story the agent sees ten inputs and either writes ten lines or silently picks - and silent picking is the thing you told me never to do. With Story, clustering is an explicit step someone owns and can get wrong visibly. Real object, or overbuilding?
